stimulus.title: Big Book Sale
stimulus.bodyText: Library Notice: Our old books need new homes! Come to the book sale in the library on Friday afternoon. Every story book costs one dollar. Every picture book costs fifty cents. Bring a bag for your books. All the money will buy new computers for the library. Sorry, we cannot take money on Thursday.

questions.prompt: Why did the library write this notice?
How much does one picture book cost?
What will happen to the money from the sale?

stimulus.title: A Note on the Kitchen Table
stimulus.bodyText:
Hi Nora,
I am at the doctor with Grandma, so I will be home at six. There is rice and chicken soup in the fridge. Please warm it up for you and Danny. Do your homework first, then you can watch TV. Do not open the door for anyone. Call me if the soup is finished.
Love, Mum

questions.prompt: Why did Mum write this note?
What must Nora do before she watches TV?

stimulus.title: The Race Around the Lake
stimulus.bodyText: Every summer, the children in Blue Park have a bike race around the lake. This year, Mimi wanted to win. She cleaned her bike and checked the tyres on Friday. On Saturday, twelve children waited at the start line. When the whistle blew, Mimi rode fast, and soon she was second. Near the big tree, she heard a shout behind her. A small boy named Sam had fallen off his bike. His knee was bleeding and his chain was off. Mimi looked at the finish line, and then she stopped. She helped Sam stand up and put his chain back on. They rode the last part together and came in last. Mimi did not get the cup, but the park guard gave her a bright red badge for helping. Her mum put the badge on the wall at home. Mimi says she will race again next summer.

questions.prompt: What is the story mainly about?
Why did Mimi stop near the big tree?
What did Mimi get after the race?
In the story, what does 'came in last' mean?

stimulus.title: Rosa's First Pancakes
stimulus.bodyText: Rosa wanted to make pancakes for her dad's birthday. She was ten, and she had never cooked alone before. On Sunday morning, she read her grandma's recipe card twice. First she mixed flour, milk and one egg in a big bowl. Then she poured a little butter into the hot pan. Her first pancake was black on one side and wet in the middle. Rosa nearly gave up. She sat down and looked at the pan for a minute. Then she remembered the words on the card: 'Cook on low heat.' She turned the heat down and tried again. The next pancake was round and golden. Rosa made six more and put strawberries on top. When her dad came into the kitchen, he smelled something sweet. He ate three pancakes and asked for the recipe. Rosa smiled and told him her secret: be patient with the heat.

questions.prompt: What is the story mainly about?
What did Rosa do just before she cooked her second pancake?
How did Rosa's dad feel about the pancakes?
In the story, what does 'gave up' mean?

stimulus.title: The Heavy Bags
stimulus.bodyText: Mr Paulo lived next door to Nate. He was old and walked slowly with a stick. Every Tuesday he went to the market and came home with two heavy bags. One Tuesday, Nate looked out of the window and saw Mr Paulo stop on the path. The bags were on the ground, and Mr Paulo was holding his back. Nate ran outside without his shoes. He carried both bags into Mr Paulo's kitchen and put the milk in the fridge. Mr Paulo wanted to give him some money, but Nate shook his head. 'I only live next door,' he said. After that day, Nate went to the market with Mr Paulo every Tuesday. They talked about football and old buses on the way. In May, Mr Paulo gave Nate a small wooden boat. He made the boat himself. Nate keeps it on his desk, next to his books.

questions.prompt: What is the story mainly about?
What did Mr Paulo give Nate in May?

stimulus.title: Life in a Hot, Dry Place
stimulus.bodyText: A camel can walk in the desert for days without a drink. How does it do this? First, a camel has a big lump on its back called a hump. The hump is not full of water. It is full of fat, and fat is stored food. When a camel cannot find plants to eat, its body uses the fat in the hump. Second, a camel can drink a lot of water very quickly. A thirsty camel drinks more than one hundred litres in about ten minutes. Third, a camel's body loses very little water, because it does not sweat much. A camel also has thick eyelashes and can close its nose. These keep the sand out when the wind is strong. Its wide feet do not sink into the soft sand. Camels help people too. In some countries, they carry heavy bags and give milk to families. The desert is hard, but the camel is ready for it.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
What is inside a camel's hump?
In the passage, what does 'hump' mean?
Why is it useful for a camel to close its nose?

stimulus.title: Colours in the Sky
stimulus.bodyText: After the rain, you sometimes see a big arc of colours in the sky. This is a rainbow. Sunlight looks white, but it is really a mix of many colours. When sunlight goes into a drop of rain, the light bends. Each colour bends a different amount, so the colours spread out. Then the light hits the back of the drop and turns back to us. We say the light reflects, and reflect means to turn back, like a ball off a wall. Millions of drops do this at the same time, so we see red, orange, yellow, green, blue and violet. To find a rainbow, stand with the sun behind you and look at the rain in front of you. Rainbows are easiest to see in the morning or late afternoon. You can also make a small rainbow at home. Spray water in the garden on a sunny day and keep your back to the sun.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
Where should the sun be when you look for a rainbow?
In the passage, what does 'reflect' mean?
Why do we see many different colours in a rainbow?

stimulus.title: The Plant That Grows Fastest
stimulus.bodyText: Bamboo looks like a tree, but it is really a kind of grass. It is the fastest-growing plant on Earth. Some kinds of bamboo can grow ninety centimetres in one day. That is too slow for your eyes to see, but if you measure a young plant in the morning and again at night, the number will change. Bamboo grows in warm, wet places in Asia, Africa and South America. It has a hollow stem, and hollow means empty in the middle, like a straw. This makes bamboo light but very strong. People cut bamboo and build houses, bridges, chairs, baskets and even bicycles with it. Cooks put young bamboo shoots in soup, and pandas eat bamboo leaves all day. Bamboo is also good for the land. When you cut a bamboo stem, the roots stay alive and send up a new stem. So one bamboo field can give people wood again and again.

questions.prompt: What is the passage mainly about?
How much can some kinds of bamboo grow in one day?
